sections.h2: Which Kenton County offices touch your tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share the job here. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns value, the Kenton County Sheriff mails and collects, and the Kenton County Clerk inherits any bill still open after April 15.

The PVA says plainly that it neither sets rates nor creates taxing districts nor takes payments. Escrow questions and bill questions go to the sheriff, while the summer sale and delinquent lists belong to the clerk. The rate itself comes from the school district, city, county and fire district named on the bill.

The county has two seats, Covington and Independence, and the offices mirror that. The PVA's Covington office is at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 3300, weekdays 8:15 to 4:15. Its Independence office is at 5272 Madison Pike, weekdays 8 to 4 and shut from 1 to 2. One number, 859-392-1750, serves both.

sections.h2: What is the Kenton County tax collection schedule?
sections.html:
Collection runs from October 1 to April 15. The best price is the first window, which ends November 1 and trims 2 percent off the face amount, and penalties begin in January.

Kenton County Sheriff collection schedule
Payment windowAmount due
October 1 to November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 10 percent plus 10 percent

Source: Kenton County Sheriff, Frequently Asked Questions. A weekend or holiday on April 15 pushes the close to the next business day.

Payment options include the sheriff's Covington counter (1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 1200), the Independence courthouse, Heritage Bank branches for cash or checks, the mail, and card or e-check payment online for a convenience fee. Mortgage escrow works too. Bounced checks cost $50. No bill in hand by October 15? Phone 859-392-1800.

sections.h2: How low is the Kenton County rate, and what does a bill include?
sections.html:
The county's slice is thin. In August 2025 the Fiscal Court voted to lower its real property rate from 12.5 to 11.5 cents per $100 of valuation, a fifth straight annual cut and the lowest since 1983.

The county's example makes the point: a home valued at $275,000 pays $316.25 to the county. The rest of the bill comes from bodies the Fiscal Court does not control. The county names school districts, the health department, the library and fire protection districts.

Cities add their own taxes. The sheriff's property tax page offers a phone list for city tax collections and notes that Morning View has no city taxes. Ask the sheriff for a line-by-line breakdown on any specific address.

For scale, the Census survey for 2020 to 2024 shows a $244,400 median value, and 70.7 percent of households own.

sections.h2: What is the review and appeal path in Kenton County?
sections.html:
Open with a review request to the PVA. The office accepts them any time after January 1, and that request doubles as the mandatory conference that precedes a formal appeal.

Conferences run by email or in person by appointment, and the Review Request Form can be filed online, in person or by phone. Proof is the owner's job, and the PVA's supporting documentation list shows what counts. Sales dashboards and a comparable sales map for houses and condominiums are posted on its site. Nothing is accepted after the inspection period closes.

  • The formal inspection period starts the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days.
  • For 2026 the PVA posted May 18 at 4:15 PM as the end of the conference period and May 20 at 4 PM as the filing deadline with the clerk.
  • A conference record, Form 62A307, must accompany any filing with the clerk.

The Board of Assessment Appeals is separate from the PVA and runs through the County Clerk's office. A loss there can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, which answers to neither the PVA nor any taxing authority.

sections.h2: Which Kenton County areas has the PVA been reviewing?
sections.html:
The PVA's published Quadrennial Review Plan covers 2023 through 2026, so field inspections have moved through the county in stages. Each parcel gets a physical look at least every four years.

The PVA's home page carries a notice for owners in Elsmere, Erlanger, Fort Mitchell, Lakeside Park and Park Hills that inspectors are working their areas, and it lists the sales behind the 2026 re-evaluation for Bromley, Covington and Ludlow. The office also values about 5,000 commercial and industrial properties and prices motor vehicles at January 1 using NADA figures.

Anyone turning 65 in 2026 may qualify for a homestead reduction, and applications go in online. The exemption belongs to the owner and not the house, so a buyer applies separately after a sale. Totally disabled owners can apply as well. Business personal property returns are due May 15, with no relief from a tax filing extension.

sections.h2: What if a Kenton County bill is not paid by April 15?
sections.html:
Once April 15 passes, the sheriff stops and the Kenton County Clerk picks up the file. The bill turns into a certificate of delinquency with a lien, and fees plus 1 percent monthly interest pile on.

The clerk's yearly sale is held in July. A bill still open then can be sold to an outside buyer, and redeeming it costs substantially more. State revenue officials show the climb with a $1,000 example: $1,254 on transfer and roughly $1,388 if paid at the clerk's counter within five business days, before the county attorney's fee applies.

  • The county attorney's first notice goes out in the month after transfer.
  • A newspaper ad and a website list name the delinquent parcels ahead of the sale.
  • The sale is set 90 to 135 days after the clerk receives the bill.

For a seller, the practical point is simple: clear any old certificate before listing so the payoff does not surprise you at closing.

sections.h2: What should a Kenton County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
A bill that arrives after a sale may still show the former owner, or both owners. The sheriff explains that the seller credits their share to the buyer or escrow agent at closing, and the owner of record then pays the whole bill.

Kenton ranks third in Kentucky by population, at 169,064 in 2020 and an estimated 175,779 in July 2025. Its 160 land square miles lie where the Licking meets the Ohio, and I-71, I-75 and I-275 all cross it. The county counts 74,593 housing units and a median household income of $80,548.

Median gross rent is $1,069 and 681 building permits were issued in 2025. Five school districts serve the county, from dense northern cities to rural southern areas. Thomas More University is the only college wholly inside the county, and Gateway Community and Technical College holds classes at sites in Covington and Park Hills among other places.

Industrial growth also feeds the tax base. Wikipedia reports that in October 2026 Niagara Bottling announced a $141 million beverage plant in Elsmere, on 52 acres at the C5 Airport East Logistics Center, with 60 full-time jobs.

faqs.q: When are Kenton County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 1 for the 2 percent discount. Face amount is due through December 31, penalties begin January 1 and the sheriff stops on April 15.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Kenton County property tax?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's Covington or Independence counters, a Heritage Bank branch, by mail to P.O. Box 188070 in Erlanger, online, or through mortgage escrow.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Kenton County tax bill is wrong?
faqs.a: The PVA at 859-392-1750 handles value and exemptions. The sheriff handles the bill itself, and the PVA neither collects nor sets rates.

faqs.q: What is the Kenton County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: A PVA conference must happen inside the 13-day May inspection window, and the clerk filing is due one working day after the window closes.

faqs.q: What is the Kenton County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Fiscal Court lowered its real property rate to 11.5 cents per $100 in August 2025. School, city, library, health and fire levies are billed on top.
